name: game capture and recording software
title: Best Game Capture and Recording Software in 2026
summary_line: Ten recorders for saving gameplay on PC, from automatic highlight clippers to free open source tools, ranked by fit for players who share clips.
definition: Game capture and recording software saves gameplay video from a PC while you play, either as continuous recordings or as short clips of recent moments. Most tools add editing, a clip library or sharing links, and many use the graphics card to keep frame-rate loss low.
intro: Recording a game sounds simple, yet the tools differ sharply in how they work: some run in the background and clip a great play for you, some record only when you press a key, some belong to a graphics driver, and one dates from 2013. This page ranks ten options for a player who wants local recordings, quick clips and an easy way to post them. The reading covered each vendor's homepage, help center and download page, with attention to price, platform and what the vendor says about editing and sharing. We did not measure performance, so none of these entries claims lower frame-rate loss than another. Where a price is missing from the pages we opened, the entry says so.

criteria.heading: Automatic clips versus manual recording
criteria.text: A few apps watch the game and save highlights without a hotkey, while others record only when you start them. Automatic capture suits players who forget to hit record after a clutch moment; manual recording suits people producing longer videos. Look at what the vendor says about detecting plays and which games that applies to, because coverage is often a short list. A tool that clips only four games helps little if you play something else.

criteria.heading: Where the footage ends up
criteria.text: Some recorders keep files on your own drive and stop there, which is simple and private. Others host clips, give you a sharing link, or send them to a community feed. Hosting is convenient, yet it ties your library to the vendor's service and terms. Decide whether you want raw files for your own editor or a one-click post, and pick the tool that matches, since switching libraries later means moving every clip by hand.

criteria.heading: Dependence on a particular graphics card
criteria.text: Driver-bundled recorders only work with that maker's hardware. That is fine if you own the matching card and wasteful if you plan to switch brands. General tools run on any card but may use more of your system. Read each platform line closely, since the cleanest-looking option may quietly require specific hardware, and confirm the card before you rely on it.

criteria.heading: Age and upkeep of the software
criteria.text: Recording tools sit close to the operating system and game engines, so stale releases can break on new games or Windows builds. We checked for release dates and vendor activity where the pages showed them. A free price tag does not help if the last update predates the games you play, so the freshness note in each entry matters. Where we found no date, we say that too.

market_notes: Of the ten tools ranked, two are open source or free for good (OBS Studio and ShareX), three offer a free tier with paid extras (Medal, Outplayed and Allstar), three sell a free version or a trial beside a paid one (Bandicam, Mirillis Action and Fraps), and two ship as part of a graphics-card driver (NVIDIA App and AMD Software Adrenalin). None of the paid options states a price on the pages we opened, and Fraps has a newest release dated February 2013.

The trade-off in this niche is convenience against control. Automatic clippers such as Outplayed and Allstar save moments for you but limit the games they cover or host the files; open tools like OBS Studio and ShareX hand you raw files and a lot of settings. Windows dominates the platform lists: Bandicam, Mirillis Action, Fraps, ShareX and both driver apps are Windows, while OBS Studio is the one option that also covers macOS and Linux.

how_to_choose.title: Decide between clips and long recordings
how_to_choose.text: If you want short moments to post, favor tools that capture automatically or hold a clip library, such as Outplayed, Medal or Allstar. If you record full sessions for editing, favor OBS Studio, Bandicam or Mirillis Action. Mixing the two is common: a clipper for highlights and a general recorder for tutorials or commentary videos, each doing the job it is built for.

how_to_choose.title: Check your graphics card first
how_to_choose.text: Open the driver app you already have installed. If it is NVIDIA or AMD, it likely includes a capture feature at no cost, so test that before downloading anything. Only add a third-party recorder if the driver feature lacks editing, hosting or the game you play. This saves an install and keeps your background processes low and your startup list short.

how_to_choose.title: Test one clip from your main game
how_to_choose.text: Record a few minutes in the game you play most, then save a clip, trim it and share it. Look at file size, how long the export takes and whether the tool kept its overlay out of the footage. Do this with two candidates, because defaults differ and a tool that works for one game can disappoint in another, so repeat the check per title.

faqs.q: What is the best game capture and recording software in 2026?
faqs.a: Outplayed is our first pick for players who want automatic highlight capture with a built-in editor and a free tier. Medal is better if you mainly want fast clip sharing, and the NVIDIA App is better for GeForce owners who prefer a driver-level recorder with no extra install.

faqs.q: Is there free software to record PC gameplay?
faqs.a: Yes. OBS Studio is free and open source on Windows, macOS and Linux, and ShareX is free with no ads on Windows. Medal says it is free to record, edit and share clips on PC, Allstar describes its clip capture as free, and Outplayed has a Free tier with ads.

Outplayed says it automatically captures a player's best moments and biggest plays. Allstar describes clip capture for Counter-Strike 2, League of Legends, Fortnite and Dota 2. Medal records, edits and shares clips, but the page we read does not say how it triggers them, so check its settings.

faqs.q: Do I need a special graphics card to record gameplay?
faqs.a: Not for general tools like OBS Studio, Bandicam or Mirillis Action. Driver recorders do tie you to hardware: the NVIDIA App lists ShadowPlay for NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD Software Adrenalin supports AMD products. If you own neither, pick a general recorder instead.

Only for specific cases. The Fraps download page lists release 3.5.99 dated February 26, 2013, and the vendor page does not say the product is discontinued. It records games using DirectX or OpenGL and shows frame rate, but newer tools get more recent updates.

faqs.q: Can I record on a Mac or Linux?
faqs.a: OBS Studio is the option here that lists macOS 13 or newer and Linux. ShareX is Windows only on the page we read, and Bandicam, Mirillis Action, Fraps, Medal and the two driver apps are PC or Windows products. Mac and Linux players should start with OBS Studio.

The Mirillis Action homepage offers a free trial download and Buy Mirillis Action options, but the page we opened did not show a price. It lists recording at 120 FPS with low CPU usage and runs on Windows Vista through Windows 11. Check the checkout page for the current figure.

tools.name: Outplayed
tools.best_for: Players who forget to hit record
tools.pricing: Free and Premium tiers. Premium removes ads and unlocks premium features; prices were not on the opened page.
tools.platforms: PC; Android (per the vendor's icon set)
tools.summary: Outplayed records your best plays by itself, adds an editor and performance tracking, and offers a Free tier with a Premium upgrade.
tools.verdict: Outplayed is a capture app that automatically records a player's best moments and biggest plays while they play. Its homepage lists game capture, performance tracking and a video editor, so the clip, the trim and the stats live in one place. A Free tier exists, and Premium removes ads and unlocks premium features. We rank it first because the automatic capture removes the biggest failure in clipping, which is missing the moment, and because it costs nothing to start.
tools.weaknesses: The Free tier carries ads, and the page we opened did not publish Premium prices. Automatic capture depends on game support, and the vendor page lists PC with an Android icon set, not macOS or Linux.
tools.wrong_for: If you want full-session recordings with fine control, use OBS Studio. Players who prefer a driver recorder with no extra install should look at the NVIDIA App.

sources.fact: Outplayed is a capture app for gamers that automatically captures their best moments and biggest plays while they play.
Outplayed offers a Free tier and a Premium tier, and says Premium removes ads and unlocks premium features.
Outplayed's homepage lists game capture, performance tracking and a video editor as features.

tools.name: Medal
tools.tagline: Free clip recorder with editing and sharing
tools.best_for: Quick clips to post to friends
tools.pricing: Free to download and use on PC, per the homepage meta description.
tools.summary: Medal is a free PC app for recording, editing and sharing game clips, with a games library behind it.
tools.verdict: Medal presents itself as a tool to record, edit and share gaming clips and gameplay videos, and its homepage description says all three are free on PC. The feature list adds clip editing, clip sharing and a games library. For a player whose goal is a link to drop into a group chat, the path from play to post is short. It sits second because it is the easiest sharing tool we read about, while Outplayed adds automatic capture and statistics.
tools.weaknesses: The facts we gathered mention PC only and give no technical specifications, supported-game list or paid tiers, so the long-term cost is unclear. Clips live in a hosted library, which suits sharing but not heavy local editing.
tools.wrong_for: Players who want raw files and total control should pick OBS Studio. For a tool that detects highlights automatically, look at Outplayed.

sources.fact: Medal is a tool to record, edit and share gaming clips and gameplay videos.
Medal's homepage description says it is free to record, edit and share gaming clips on PC.

tools.name: NVIDIA App
tools.best_for: GeForce owners who want no extra install
tools.pricing: The download page is region-specific and shows no price.
tools.summary: The NVIDIA App bundles ShadowPlay and driver updates, so GeForce owners can record without installing a separate recorder at all.
tools.verdict: NVIDIA calls the app the essential companion for PC gamers and creators, used to keep drivers up to date. The download page names NVIDIA ShadowPlay and the Broadcast App among its features, so capture arrives alongside the drivers you already need. For anyone with a supported card, the best first step is to test it, since the cost is a settings change. It ranks third because it is convenient and tied to NVIDIA hardware, which limits who gains from it.
tools.weaknesses: It requires an NVIDIA GPU on a Windows PC, and the page we read states no price or limits. The vendor lists ShadowPlay by name only, so details on clip length or sharing are missing from our facts.
tools.wrong_for: AMD or integrated-graphics owners should use AMD Software Adrenalin or OBS Studio instead. Players who want hosted clip libraries could try Medal.

sources.fact: The NVIDIA App is described by NVIDIA as the essential companion for PC gamers and creators, used to keep drivers up to date.
The NVIDIA App download page lists NVIDIA ShadowPlay and the Broadcast App among its features.
NVIDIA's download page for the NVIDIA App is available by region and does not show a price.

tools.name: OBS Studio
tools.tagline: Free open source recorder for any desktop
tools.platforms: Windows 10 and 11, macOS 13 or newer, Linux
tools.summary: OBS Studio records on Windows, macOS and Linux for free, with scenes built from game, window and webcam sources.
tools.verdict: The OBS project describes its software as free and open source for video recording and live streaming. Scenes can combine window captures, browser windows, webcams and capture cards, so one file can hold gameplay and a face camera. Platform support covers Windows 10 and 11, macOS 13 or newer and Linux. It is a good fit for tutorial makers and anyone who wants raw files for their own editor, which is why it holds fourth place.
tools.weaknesses: Nothing about clipping, highlights or sharing appears in the vendor facts, so it is a recorder, not a clip service. Setup is manual: sources, audio and output settings are yours to configure before the first recording.
tools.wrong_for: A player who only wants a one-click highlight should choose Outplayed or Medal. Anyone who records a long session and expects a clip library will be disappointed.

sources.fact: OBS (Open Broadcaster Software) is free and open source software for video recording and live streaming.
The homepage says OBS supports Windows 10 and Windows 11, macOS 13.0 or newer, and Linux.
The homepage describes scenes made of multiple sources including window captures, browser windows, webcams and capture cards.

tools.name: Mirillis Action
tools.tagline: Windows recorder for HD, 4K and HDR
tools.pricing: The homepage offers a free trial download and a purchase option; prices were not on the opened page.
tools.summary: Mirillis Action from Mirillis records games and the desktop at up to 120 FPS, with 4K webcam and HDR options, on Windows.
tools.verdict: Mirillis describes Mirillis Action as screen and game recording software that also streams, with webcam and microphone support. The homepage states it can record at 120 FPS with low CPU usage, and the feature list adds HDR and 4K webcam. It runs on Windows Vista, 7, 8.1, 10 and 11, a long span. The free trial means you can check smoothness on your own machine before paying, which earns it fifth place.
tools.weaknesses: The page we opened did not show a price, only a trial download and Buy Mirillis Action options. The vendor site is mirillis.com, and the /action path returned 404, so product details may move. Windows only.
tools.wrong_for: Mac and Linux players should use OBS Studio. Anyone who wants a price shown up front should compare Bandicam or the free ShareX.

sources.fact: Action is screen and game recording software that records and streams desktop, apps and games with webcam and microphone.
Action's homepage states it can record video at 120 FPS with low CPU usage and offers a download to try for free.
Action runs on Windows Vista, 7, 8.1, 10 and 11, per the vendor homepage.

tools.name: Bandicam
tools.tagline: Windows screen, game and webcam recorder
tools.best_for: Windows users wanting AI tools and editing
tools.pricing: Bandicam has a free version and a full version; the homepage links to a free vs full version comparison. Prices were not on the opened pages.
tools.summary: Bandicam captures the screen, gameplay and webcam on Windows, with built-in editing, an audio recorder and AI tools.
tools.verdict: Bandicam is screen recording software for capturing the PC screen, gameplay and webcam, according to its homepage, with built-in editing and AI tools plus an audio recorder. It exists in a free and a full version, and the homepage links to a comparison page, so you can see what the free one leaves out before buying. It lands sixth because it covers more than games, yet the vendor facts include no frame-rate claims or game-specific features.
tools.weaknesses: Prices were not on the pages we opened, so the cost of the full version is unknown. Windows is the only platform in our facts, and the free version's limits sit on a comparison page we did not read in detail.
tools.wrong_for: If you want automatic highlights, use Outplayed. For a no-cost open alternative that covers more systems, use OBS Studio.

sources.fact: Bandicam is screen recording software for capturing the PC screen, gameplay and webcam, with built-in editing and AI tools.
Bandicam's homepage links to a Free vs Full version page, so it is offered in both a free and a full version.

tools.name: Allstar
tools.tagline: Free clip capture for four competitive games
tools.pricing: The homepage calls clip capture free; subscriptions and product tiers exist but no prices appeared on the pages opened.
tools.platforms: Desktop app, plus iOS and Android apps
tools.summary: Allstar describes free clip capture with zero FPS drop for Counter-Strike 2, League of Legends, Fortnite and Dota 2, with apps on iOS and Android.
tools.verdict: The homepage says Allstar offers free, fast and easy clip capture for four named games. The help center lists Allstar Studio, Montages, Clip Feed and AllstarBot as product areas, and mentions mobile apps for iOS and Android. It suits players of those four titles who want a hosted place for highlights and montages. It sits seventh because the game list is narrow compared with general recorders, and the vendor leaves prices to a billing section.
tools.weaknesses: Game coverage on the homepage is four titles, which excludes most libraries. The help center mentions subscriptions and product tiers but we saw no prices, and the main site rendered little text, so details are thin.
tools.wrong_for: Players outside those four games should pick OBS Studio or Medal. Those wanting driver-level capture should check the NVIDIA App.

sources.fact: The homepage describes Allstar as free, fast and easy clip capture with zero FPS drop for Counter-Strike 2, League of Legends, Fortnite and Dota 2.
The help center lists Allstar Studio, Montages, Clip Feed and AllstarBot as product areas, and says Allstar is available as an iOS and Android app.
The help center has a Billing and Subscriptions section about Allstar subscriptions and product tiers, and its footer reads Allstar Gaming, Inc.

tools.name: AMD Software Adrenalin
tools.tagline: Driver software with in-game capture for AMD
tools.pricing: No price is shown; the vendor page presents it as software for AMD products.
tools.summary: AMD Software Adrenalin bundles driver updates, game stats and in-game capture for AMD products on a Windows PC.
tools.verdict: AMD says its Adrenalin Edition gives access to software features, game stats and driver updates, and lets users configure, launch or view installed games from one location and capture in-game moments. Radeon owners already have it installed, so recording starts without a new download. It is a practical first test for those users, but it ranks eighth because it ships as a driver suite, and the vendor page gives no capture specifications.
tools.weaknesses: It works only with AMD products on a Windows PC. The page we read lists in-game capture as one line and gives no format, length or sharing details, so judging quality needs a test on your own system.
tools.wrong_for: Anyone with an NVIDIA card should look at the NVIDIA App. Players who want editing and hosting should compare Medal.

sources.fact: AMD Software Adrenalin Edition is an application for AMD products that gives access to software features, game stats and driver updates.
The AMD page says the app lets users configure, launch or view installed games from one location and capture in-game moments.

tools.name: ShareX
tools.tagline: Free Windows screenshot and screen-recording tool
tools.best_for: Free screen video and GIFs on Windows
tools.pricing: Completely free, with no advertisements; the footer says 'Free forever. Open source. No account required.' A Donate page is linked.
tools.platforms: Windows (the page names Windows only; a macOS and Linux artifacts link appears without details)
tools.summary: ShareX is a free, open source Windows tool for screenshots, screen recording and GIFs, with automation after capture.
tools.verdict: ShareX is described by its own page as a free and open source screenshot tool for Windows that also records screen video and GIFs. The page says free forever, no ads and no account, with capture modes including fullscreen, active window, region and scrolling capture, plus custom uploaders and an image editor. It fits quick bug clips and short GIFs. It ranks ninth because game recording is a side feature, not the focus.
tools.weaknesses: Windows is the only platform the page names, and gaming is not its main purpose, so it offers no automatic highlight capture. Screen recording sits beside screenshots, and the vendor page does not state game-specific performance claims.
tools.wrong_for: Players who want highlight clipping should use Outplayed. For a full recorder with scenes and a webcam layer, pick OBS Studio instead.

sources.fact: ShareX is a free and open source screenshot tool for Windows, according to the vendor home page.
The vendor page says the software is completely free with no advertisements, and free forever, open source and requires no account.
The vendor page lists capture modes including fullscreen, active window, region, scrolling capture and screen recording.
The vendor page carries the copyright line 'Copyright © 2007-2026 ShareX Team' and says it has over 18 years of active development.

tools.name: Fraps
tools.tagline: Veteran Windows recorder with FPS counter
tools.best_for: Benchmark overlays on DirectX or OpenGL games
tools.pricing: A free download is offered; the paid full version requires registration and no price appears on the download page.
tools.summary: Fraps shows frame rate, takes screenshots and records video in DirectX and OpenGL games on Windows, with a last release in 2013.
tools.verdict: Fraps is a Windows utility for showing frame rates, taking screenshots and recording video in games that use DirectX or OpenGL. The vendor lists real-time capture up to 7680x4800 and 1 to 120 fps, plus custom benchmarks and saved statistics. A free download lets you try it, and a paid unrestricted full version requires registration. Its value today is mostly the on-screen FPS counter, which explains the last-place ranking.
tools.weaknesses: The download page gives the latest release as Fraps 3.5.99, dated February 26, 2013, so newer games and Windows builds may not be supported. The vendor does not say it is discontinued, and no full-version price appears.
tools.wrong_for: Anyone recording current games should choose OBS Studio or Bandicam. Players wanting clip tools that still get regular updates should try Outplayed.

sources.fact: Fraps is a universal Windows application for showing frame rates, taking screenshots and recording video in games that use DirectX or OpenGL.
The vendor page says 'fraps' and 'beepa' are registered trademarks of Beepa Pty Ltd.
The vendor page offers a free download and describes a paid unrestricted full version that requires registration.
The download page gives the latest release as Fraps 3.5.99, dated February 26th, 2013.
